prompt:
Animate our original illustrated character Rich Cash from the supplied first frame. ONE continuous NINE-second fixed-camera shot, natural real-time speed. Preserve the exact stocky jowly man, brown toupee/gray sides, cream knit polo, gold watch, trousers, cream telephone, terrace and Siamese cat. Keep camera absolutely locked, identical scale and position, no zoom, pan, cuts or split-screen. Remain seated, gestures within the existing shoulder/elbow area for later half-frame cropping.
COMEDY ACTING PREMISE: this pompous wealthy man hears a cheerful caller reveal evidence that could ruin his reputation and SEND HIM TO JAIL. He suddenly imagines losing EVERYTHING. His attempted dignity collapses into unmistakable farcical panic. This is social comedy in bright daylight, not horror, physical danger, anger or an enjoyable surprise. The audience laughs at how spectacularly this self-important man loses his nerve.
0–1s: already holding receiver to ear, listen with a neutral impatient expression, slight breathing and eye movement. Do not grin. Keep this setup very brief.
1–2.5s: the information lands. His eyes widen sharply, both eyebrows rise high, jaw drops into a small alarmed O, chin recoils and shoulders jump. Clear shocked realization: she KNOWS. His lips never curl up into a smile.
2.5–4.5s: panic rapidly escalates. He leans slightly forward, clutches the receiver, eyes dart once left and right checking for witnesses. A few small glistening sweat beads appear on his forehead and temples. His free hand lifts to chest height, palm outward in an urgent pleading WAIT gesture, fingers trembling slightly. Mouth makes short desperate attempts to interrupt; eyebrows remain lifted and pinched inward with worry. No angry scowl.
4.5–6.5s: composure completely gone. Free hand makes two quick compact pleading stop gestures toward the caller he cannot see, then briefly dabs his sweating temple with the back of that hand. His chin pulls into his neck, shoulders hunch, eyes stay wide; an exaggerated nervous gulp makes the predicament funny. Keep receiver pressed to ear in its original hand. No new handkerchief or props.
6.5–8s: his free hand hovers helplessly near his chest while he visibly stammers, open mouth corners pulled DOWN, lower lip tense, brows raised in desperate appeal. He looks trapped and imploring, almost begging her to stop. Sustain the high comic panic, do not resolve it into relief. Small sweat beads remain, not streams or fountains.
8–9s: living tail of tense breathing, worried eyes and trembling free hand. End STILL PANICKED. Never smile, smirk, laugh, look pleased, regain confidence or relax after the realization. No horror lighting, screaming face distortion, grotesque features, tears or injury. Preserve recognizable facial anatomy while making the acting bold enough to read at half-screen size.
The humor comes from dignified authority unraveling. The Siamese stays seated on its chair, giving only a restrained unimpressed blink; secondary to Rich. Keep coherent hands, attached coiled cord, stable telephone and furniture. No hang-up, hand switching, standing, extra people, text or music. Silent conversational mouth motion; music replaces generated audio. Main reaction develops by second6 with continuation for edit handles.
